metadata.title: OpenLogic : édition française — Des ensembles à la logique du premier ordre
metadata.subject: Ensembles, relations, fonctions, dénombrabilité, nombres, logique propositionnelle et logique du premier ordre, séquents, déduction naturelle, tableaux et déduction axiomatique
metadata.author: Open Logic Project ; traduction française assistée par IA

visual_inspection.scope: All front-matter pages and every physical page containing the new chapter, plus the following chapter transition.

notes: Physical pages 88–96 contain printed pages 84–92 of Chapter 8; physical page 97 begins Chapter 9.
The two external forward references are visibly labeled as original-English material outside this delivery.
The exercise count remains 106 because the new introductory chapter contains no exercises.

content_diagnostic.finding: All 45 unmatched windows on physical pages 88–96 are PDF extraction artifacts involving an adjacent formula, the inline footnote, |M|, TeX set braces or a joined predicate symbol. The target source, PDF, native MathML and rendered EPUB contain the corresponding prose.

visual_review.finding: Front matter, contents, all nine new sections, the following chapter transition and bibliography were inspected at desktop and mobile widths. Text, headings, formulas, links and notes are legible. The inherited wide derivation tables expose their rightmost columns through local horizontal panning.

repairs: Inherited verified MathML, link, footnote, namespace and duplicate-ID repairs
Empty exercise headings/navigation removed for the two chapters without exercises
Chapter titles and release metadata updated for the inserted first-order introduction
Wide equations and derivation tables retained inside local horizontal scrollers
Regenerated SVGs verified canonically identical after normalizing internal identifiers

quality_reaudit.sample_limit: Nine sampled pages as requested; not a fresh line-by-line audit of every page in the three chapters.

units.declared_source_correction: Three malformed quantifier/body boundaries are restored so that the universal formula closes after the conditional.
Predicates, not constants, may have multiple places; the example assignment takes values in the already fixed domain {0,1,2}, not {1,2,3}.
Malformed macro boundaries in the opening universal formula are restored.
